architectQuestion: Should backfillIndex treat a live claim as decide does? Yes. Its record write takes the claimant's revision, the claimant's outcome write loses its compare-and-set, and the delivery is asked for again. Both reviews reproduced this. So the back-fill must Put only the claim-end entry, as decide does.

keyFindings.description: backfillIndex writes the record of an older build's live claim (no Pending), which moves the revision the claimant's outcome write depends on. That write loses its compare-and-set, and the delivery is requested again (reproduced by both reviews). This is reachable through an older build's operator command, which takes no lease, or through a lease lost mid-pass. It runs on every sweep under an older-build cursor and on every marker expiry. Fix: for a record under a live claim, Put pendingFor's entry and skip the record write, as decide does, ideally through one shared helper. Add the reproduction as a test.

Only a complete sweep writes the cursor. So an older build whose sweeps never complete (cut short by SIGTERM, the 300-request cap, or a rate limit) leaves an indexed:true cursor and the marker set. A record it created, refused and at the far edge of Lookback, is then read by nothing until the marker expires, up to 72 h (the deep review reproduced 40 sweeps with no request). Fix: give the marker a time and back-fill again once it is older than Lookback (one full scan an hour at most), and correct the olderBuild comment.

TestAStrayIndexEntryIsDeletedOnlyPastTheMargin passes with strayMargin = cursorOverlap (both reviews), so the extra minute is not pinned. Put the clock off a minute boundary and add a stray keyed at minute(now) - cursorOverlap.
